authority: Owner directions in this development task

decisions.decision: ai-governance-regime is the organizational wrapper around the RealityEngine, aligned with the global standards and frameworks the package's documents track (ISO/IEC 42001/42005/42006, NIST AI RMF and AI 600-1, the EU AI Act, OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS and the others in SPECIFICATION.md section 2).
constraints: Alignment claims need a pinned source per framework before any machine cites it.

decisions.decision: This domain is the proof of workflow for new domain production: each factory step is carried out and recorded here, so the next domain can follow it.
constraints: Record each step's inputs, outputs and verification in PACKAGE_STATUS.md as it is done.

decisions.decision: The package follows the ifrs-accounting factory layout.
constraints: Directories appear when their step produces content; none is created empty.

decisions.decision: The canonical machines are the 17 base machines M-GOV-01..17 from SPECIFICATION.md 4.3 and HARDENING_TRANSITION_RULES.md. The governed target domain travels in the asset frame; the intake corpora's per-domain copies are not carried over.
constraints: The intake corpora stay in intake/ as received.

decisions.decision: Each machine has its own regions in the governance band (input <= 16 cells, an 8-element output); the PE composes the lifecycle and gate signals into each input, and a fixture aggregator (GOV00) folds the verdicts onto the four domain verdict elements.
constraints: The specification's cell numbers become signal provenance (inputSemantics), not regions.
The band is proposed as [16960:17429]; allocation follows the admission workflow (GOV-R04).
Corrected 2026-11-25: [16960:17439] was the 0.1.0 band; the 0.2.0 machines use [16960:17429] (PACKAGE_STATUS.md, 0.2.0 record).

decisions.decision: Before anything else changes, the machines conform to schemas/machine.schema.json and carry the CESs (one regular expression each) that represent the specified behaviors.
constraints: Checked by tools/verify_machines.py with the repository's own schema, pattern and cloneable gates.

decisions.decision: Every agentic workflow (W1-W7) and every Source in governance-sources.json is in v1 of the domain.
constraints: A Source whose producer does not exist yet is built, not dropped; until it exists its machines are tested only against interned sequences.
The hooks into approve-domain.sh, deployments and cut-release.sh are changes to those repositories, approved separately.

decisions.decision: Agent behavior is generated runtime-neutral (schemas/agent-behavior.schema.json) and rendered per runtime, so the move from OpenClaw to ACP-hosted agents changes an adapter, not the agents.
constraints: localOpenClawStack machine-behaviors/runtimes renders OpenClaw and ACP; the committed OpenClaw agents stay byte-identical.

decisions.decision: The scope stays the 18 machines GOV00-GOV17 (GOV-SD-04 reaffirmed). The received hardening workplan's 315-machine corpus, its [16960:17087] band and its fixed cells 16987-16991 are source material, not targets.
constraints: M-GOV-15/16/17 in RESOLUTION_WORKPLAN.md are GOV15/16/17 here (corpus-315's M-GOV-HRD-313..315).
Cells 16987-16991 survive only as inputSemantics provenance labels (GOV-SD-05).
The workplan's 1,867-machine and p99 <= 820 ns figures are designed, not measured (GOV-R09).

decisions.decision: Threat classification and dynamic, reactive threat observability are a separate peer domain, threat-dynamics, not part of ai-governance-regime. This domain focuses on closing the seven wrapper gaps (GAP_ANALYSIS.md).
constraints: The NIST SP 2400-102 adversarial-ML taxonomy (NISTAML attack classes, agentic .061-.067) is threat-dynamics' specification, not this domain's.
Control identifiers for this domain come from the governance frameworks pinned under GOV-R07, not from SP 2400-102.

decisions.decision: Observe vs decide: threat-dynamics owns classification, detection, red-team harnesses and vendor canaries, and publishes the results as Sources; ai-governance-regime consumes them only as gate inputs and owns the decision.
constraints: The two domains couple only through published lanes, declared on both sides (governance-sources.json producerDomain; threat-dynamics' published-lane contract).
The Sources produced by threat-dynamics: gate_redteam_pass (GOV01, gap 3), mon_canary_drift_score (GOV16, gap 6) and mon_xdomain_mu_agg (GOV16, gap 5).
Admission order: threat-dynamics, the producer, is admitted before this domain.

decisions.decision: One shared extension corpus and regression profile carries both peer domains above the corpus vector budget (16944), as MACHINE_CONCEPT.md 9.3 provides. The standard vector budget does not change.
constraints: The 8-bit watchdogs GOV07, GOV08, GOV09, GOV12, GOV14 and GOV16 reach the parity gate through this extension corpus (closes GOV-R11).
threat-dynamics is allocated next to this domain's band, below the clone space (20480).

decisions.decision: Two quorums, two terms. An approval quorum is the human q-of-n signer bundle (Byzantine bounds, signer diversity across org units); the engine quorum is RealityEngine_CI/docs/QUORUM_CONTRACT.md's unanimous C++, LSP and Scala agreement. An approval quorum never substitutes for the engine quorum.
constraints: The cross-department signer rule (RESOLUTION_WORKPLAN.md 1.3) is enforced inside GOV06, not by changing QUORUM_CONTRACT.md.
Closes GOV-R06; documents adopt the terms when next revised (GOV-R10, GOV-R22).

decisions.decision: Framework alignment follows the ifrs-accounting pattern: a source-requirements.json listing each control's obligation, required evidence and source span against a pinned edition. Which frameworks and controls are in scope, and which are out, is declared per milestone.
constraints: A framework not declared in scope for a milestone is recorded as out of scope for it, never as aligned.
The milestone scoping also stages the Source producers (GOV-SD-16).
Closes GOV-R07 as a decision; the per-milestone scope is step 3 work.

decisions.decision: The authoritative baseline is RealityEngine V0.18, NIST terminology revision (22 November 2026), pinned at intake/BASELINE-V0.18-NIST.md (the Markdown source).
constraints: The received documents cite the 19 November edition; its sha256 is recorded in admission-source-manifest.json as the cited edition.
Closes GOV-R08.
The owner's PDF rendering of the same edition is recorded by sha256 only (renderedEdition).

decisions.decision: Until a producer exists, every governance input is provided as a simulation: a Source through the ISRE, composed by the PE, carrying the Source semantics of SURFACE_SPEC Sources & Sensors (kind, region, value, activity, sensor TTL and freshness, membership).
constraints: A machine's own input sequences are not enough: they specify behavior at machine granularity, while a simulated Source has to reproduce the signal's semantics across machines and over time (e.g. a revoked key dropping lane_quorum_integrity_ok within one poll for every consumer).
Each signal in governance-sources.json gets its simulated-Source definition before its machines count as tested.
Real producers are staged by milestone (GOV-SD-14); a producer replaces its simulation without changing the consuming machines.
Closes GOV-R09 as a decision.

decisions.decision: The semantic amendments GOV-SA-01..22 are approved as proposed (owner: "use your suggestions and i approve all of them").
constraints: Including the step counts most open to judgement: SA-14 (an approval counts after the diff-shown parked state has held 2 steps) and SA-19 (a watchdog trips after 3 consecutive breach readings, 2 for GOV09; GOV08 recovers after 2 in-range readings).
Including SA-18: the approval quorum needs Risk, Engineering and Legal signatures, no preparer among the signers, and the bundle ready before the last signature.
A later change to an approved amendment is a new amendment, not an edit. threat-dynamics TD-SA-02 and TD-SA-06 mirror SA-19 and GOV16 and change with them.
Closes GOV-R14.

decisions.decision: The baseline is RealityEngine V0.19, v0.0.3 progress revision (25 November 2026), pinned at intake/BASELINE-V0.19-NIST.md. Accepted provisionally (owner: "V0.19 is provisionally accepted").
constraints: Provisional: citations move to V0.19, and V0.18 stays pinned as the prior edition until the owner's final acceptance, which is recorded as an amendment to this decision.
V0.19 changes only statuses, counts and locations against V0.18 (its Appendix E); a citation of a result, proof, hypothesis or objective reads the same in both.
Supersedes GOV-SD-15 provisionally; closes GOV-R29 provisionally.

decisions.decision: Outputs are latched. Owner, 2026-11-27: "the output is latched". On a step where a CES asserts, the engine writes the machine's whole output region with the merged vector; on a step where none asserts, the region keeps the last vector written. Observed identically on C++, LSP, Scala, Rust and Go (threat-dynamics live run 2026-11-26).
constraints: A decision output (PERMIT_DEPLOY, HALT_PROMOTION, REVOKE_EPOCH, TRIGGER_INCIDENT) would otherwise hold after its conditions end: with the package evaluator latched and no other change, 83 of the 87 fixtures that assert a decision still hold it three nominal steps later, GOV01's PERMIT_DEPLOY among them.
Addressed by GOV-SA-23 (proposed): one idle CES per machine.
The evaluator models the latch, and the GOV-SA-06 feedback cell reads the latched region.
Resolves GOV-R30.

decisions.decision: GOV-SA-23 is approved as recommended (owner: "approve it as you recommend"): every machine carries one idle CES that asserts the all-zero vector, so under latched outputs (GOV-SD-19) a decision holds exactly as long as its condition.
constraints: The alternative, accepting that a decision means the last one written and adding explicit release CESs machine by machine, is not taken: it is fail-open until every machine has one.
Live evidence: the engines write the all-zero vector identically on five engines (acceptance/live-run-2026-11-27.json).
Closes GOV-R31.

decisions.decision: V0.19 remains provisionally accepted (GOV-SD-18). The owner expects one more update to it, which will not directly affect this package's work.
constraints: Citations continue to read V0.19; V0.18 stays pinned as the prior edition until final acceptance.
The expected update is intaken and re-pinned like V0.19 when it arrives.

decisions.decision: SR latches are held as automaton state in one closed CES (GOV-SA-24), not through a feedback cell and a PE composition. Owner rules on which it rests: a CES's next-active lists may branch and cycle, with no restriction beyond non-duplication, but may never reference an event in another CES of the same or another machine, since CESs exchange information only through the machine's ISRE presentation; and outputs persist by default, a one-step output being requested specifically.
constraints: The owner chose the automaton-state route for GOV-R12 over an engine composition.
Within a CES only the initial event is always armed, so no CES can disable another; gating across CESs is only through the ISRE.

GOV-SA-04 split an `or` guard into several CESs on the reading that a CES could not branch. That reading was too strict; a single branched CES is now permissible. Revisiting SA-04 is optional (GOV-R33).
Closes GOV-R12.

decisions.decision: A CES may have more than one initial Reality Event and more than one final Reality Event: its regular expression may alternate at the start, R = (a+b)c, or at the end, R = a(b+c), as well as in the middle. Every initial event is always armed. With GOV-SD-22, the next-active rules: no duplicates, every entry within the CES.
constraints: SURFACE_SPEC's "every sequence has exactly one initial event and exactly one event without successors" is a measurement of the corpus (2026-10-24), not a rule.

Applied: GOV-SA-25 (GOV05). The package evaluator arms every initial event, and the verifier's shape check is now: one or more initial and final events, closed next-active lists without duplicates, every event reachable from an initial event.
Closes GOV-R33.

independentReview: Domain review and the admission workflow (scripts/approve-domain.sh) remain required.
